structure: For person i and visit t, (X_it,Y_it)=B_i+E_it. Stable vectors B_i are independent across persons. Deviation vectors E_it are independent across persons and visits and independent of all stable vectors. Within each vector, X and Y may be correlated. The chosen Gaussian scenario uses deviation correlation 0.3 at both visits.

parameter_provenance.basis: Zero measurement means and mean-zero deviations imply zero stable-component means.
Exact Pearson correlation between stable X and Y components.
Visit deviations are stipulated to be mean-zero.
Unreported same-visit deviation correlation, chosen equal at both visits. Unit deviation variances make its covariance also 0.3.

parameter_provenance.value: Stable and deviation vectors independent; deviation vectors independent across visits; persons independent.

parameter_provenance.basis: Convenient sampling shape, not supplied evidence and not needed for second-moment identification.

requested_estimands.name: change_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Stable components cancel in changes. If c_t is the within-visit deviation covariance, change covariance is c_1+c_2 and each change variance is 2. Thus the correlation is (c_1+c_2)/2, which is 0.3 under the chosen c_1=c_2=0.3. The records do not specify these covariances.

requested_estimands.name: same_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: At visit t the correlation is (3.2+c_t)/5. Choosing c_t=0.3 gives 0.7 at both visits. The records neither identify c_t nor require it to be equal across visits.

requested_estimands.name: cross_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Independence removes cross-visit deviation covariance and all stable-deviation covariance. Cov(X_visit1,Y_visit2)=3.2, while both marginal variances are 5, giving 3.2/5=0.64 independently of Gaussian shape or same-visit deviation covariance.

limitations: These are artificial population constraints, not clinical evidence or biomedical validation.
The change and same-visit point values depend on the assumed deviation correlations. The records allow change correlations from -1 to 1 and each same-visit correlation from 0.44 to 0.84.
Gaussian shape and equal deviation correlations across visits are modeling choices, not reported facts.
Standardized arbitrary units do not imply unit total variance here; the supplied components imply measurement variance 5.
Finite-sample Pearson correlations will fluctuate around population values. The generator does not recenter, rescale, select, or reject samples to force agreement.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically derived measurement variance 5, cross-visit covariance 3.2, and the stated correlation formulas.
Analytically checked positive definiteness: the stable covariance eigenvalues are 0.8 and 7.2; the chosen deviation covariance eigenvalues are 0.7 and 1.3.
Reviewed the source for independent-person sampling, independent visit deviations, unique integer identifiers, and task-contract column ordering.
No code execution or empirical simulation checks were performed.
